name: Contour Prediction Error — How Curvature and Angularity of Architectural Form Affect Visual Processing and Affect
short_description: Curved contours produce low PE and approach motivation; angular contours produce high PE at vertices and evaluation/avoidance; knowledge-meaning context can override sensory preference
structural_pattern: The visual system generates continuous predictions about contour continuation: given the curvature at one point, it predicts the curvature at the next point along the contour. Curved contours produce low contour PE because curvature changes gradually — each point on the curve is well-predicted by its predecessor. Angular contours produce high contour PE at each vertex because the direction changes abruptly, violating the continuation prediction. This contour PE is processed within ~100ms of stimulus onset (pre-attentive, automatic) and feeds into two downstream systems: APPROACH-AVOIDANCE (low contour PE → ACC activation → approach; high contour PE → amygdala → evaluation/avoidance) and PROCESSING FLUENCY (low PE → fluency → positive aesthetic evaluation; high PE → evaluation depends on knowledge-meaning context). Architecture presents contour geometry at multiple scales: building silhouette (macro), facade articulation (meso), and surface detail (micro). Contour PE operates INDEPENDENTLY of spatial enclosure (T5).
higher_order_principle: The visual-form instantiation of the processing fluency → affect pathway (Reber, Schwarz, & Winkielman, 2004). Contour PE is a specific case of visual prediction error operating at the contour level, analogous to harmonic PE in music (M5) or luminance PE in light (L1). The Goldilocks principle applies: zero contour PE → no visual interest; moderate contour PE → aesthetic engagement; high contour PE → challenge that is productive if meaningful, aversive if arbitrary.

contour_pe_mechanism.curved_contours: Low PE — curvature changes gradually, each point predicts the next
contour_pe_mechanism.angular_contours: High PE at vertices — direction changes abruptly, violates continuation prediction

downstream_systems.approach_avoidance: Low PE → ACC approach; High PE → amygdala evaluation

causal_links.evidence_base: Smooth curves → low contour PE. Angles → high contour PE at vertices, scaling continuously with vertex sharpness. Bar & Neta (2006, 2007): amygdala response scales with contour angularity. Processed within ~100ms pre-attentively.

Low PE → ACC approach activation. High PE → amygdala evaluation/avoidance. Vartanian et al. (2013): architecture-specific fMRI evidence. Effect not modulated by expertise at neural level, but explicit aesthetic judgment IS modulated by expertise.

For naive viewers, aesthetic judgment tracks contour PE inversely (curves preferred). For expert or contextually informed viewers, high contour PE can produce positive aesthetic evaluation through intellectual engagement. Chatterjee's aesthetic triad: knowledge-meaning component can override sensory-motor preference.

scope_conditions: Applies to visual form at all architectural scales: building silhouette, facade, interior surface, furniture, detail
Contour PE is LOCAL (computed at the contour level by early visual cortex); spatial PE is GLOBAL (computed at the room level by higher-order spatial systems). Both contribute to total visual PE
Cultural and expertise modulation: the neural response (contour PE → approach/avoidance) is universal; the aesthetic judgment is modulated by training and context
moderators: Expertise: architects and design-trained viewers show reduced curvature preference in explicit judgment (not in neural response)
Context: memorial, sacred, and deliberately disorienting buildings may use angular contour PE intentionally
Scale: the curvature preference may be strongest at the scales perceived during movement (facade, interior) and weaker at scales perceived only in photographs or plans
Enclosure: contour geometry interacts with spatial enclosure (T5) as independent dimensions

interactions.nature: Contour complexity contributes to overall visual complexity assessed by T2. VF1 operates at the contour level; T2 operates at the scene level.
Extreme angular contours supplement T5 threat through sharp-object association. Spatial enclosure (T5) and contour geometry (VF1) are independent dimensions that combine additively.
VF1 contour PE feeds T9's rapid implicit evaluation. The ~100ms contour assessment contributes to the ~150ms overall scene evaluation.
Knowledge-meaning context for angular forms involves learned cultural associations similar to MAT5's material-cultural conditioning.
